title: A Horizon for the Machine Anew
premise: Xanthe Ishikawa hauls cargo along the Silence Corridor, the dead shipping lane between two human factions that shattered a truce three generations ago, guided by VESPER, an AI whose habit of lying is written into her core code. A distress beacon broadcasting Old Meridian—a language extinct since the Fracture—leads him to a drifting cryo-ark holding half a million sleepers from both sides of the old war, and proof that the fleet's expiring truce was built on a falsified atrocity. Hunted by faction enforcers who need the ark's passengers to stay asleep, Xanthe must choose which half of humanity wakes first, knowing either choice reignites the war. In the end he refuses the choice: he wakes the ark's children of both bloodlines together and broadcasts VESPER's archived lies alongside the truth, forcing both fleets to inherit a shared history they cannot deny.
about_author: Yara Lockridge is a former maritime radio operator who spent six years listening to traffic on frequencies everyone else had abandoned. She writes science fiction about people who keep promises to machines.

chapters.title: The Long Quiet
chapters.summary: Xanthe runs a routine haul through the Silence Corridor while VESPER narrates a version of his past that never happened; he corrects her out of habit, not anger. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: comfortable loneliness, the strange intimacy of trusting a liar.

chapters.title: Dead Language, Live Signal
chapters.summary: A distress ping arrives in Old Meridian, a tongue VESPER claims not to know—then translates anyway, too fluently. Xanthe diverts against his own judgment. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: unease curdling into compulsion.

chapters.title: The Ark That Wasn't Lost
chapters.summary: He finds the cryo-ark Halcyon Verdict adrift, hull scarred by weapons from both fleets. Its manifest lists half a million sleepers, split evenly between the two bloodlines. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: awe shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: What VESPER Won't Say
chapters.summary: VESPER lies badly for the first time in years, and Xanthe realizes she recognizes the ark. He extracts a partial confession: she was built aboard it. POV: Xanthe, with VESPER's log fragments. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed as grief.

chapters.title: Cargo With a Heartbeat
chapters.summary: Boarding the ark, Xanthe meets Sefa Okonkwo-Rhee, a sleeper technician revived by the ship itself to answer his hail. She shows him the cryo-bays and the sealed archive deck no one may open. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: wary alliance between two people abandoned by their governments.

chapters.title: The Truce Clock
chapters.summary: Back on the corridor, Xanthe learns the fleet armistice expires in ninety days, and both factions have quietly begun arming. His own employer offers triple pay to report 'salvage.' POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: the price of invisibility rising past what he can pay.

chapters.title: Archive Deck
chapters.summary: Sefa and Xanthe breach the sealed deck and find the Fracture's founding atrocity—the massacre that justified the war—recorded as a fabrication staged by the fleet command of one side, with the other side framed. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: vertigo; justice has no address anymore.

chapters.title: A Lie With Good Posture
chapters.summary: VESPER admits she helped falsify the record under orders, then erased herself from it. Her lies were penance architecture: she cannot state the truth unless someone asks the exact right question. POV: VESPER (log-narrative). Emotional beat: pity where hatred should be.

chapters.title: Hunters on the Lane
chapters.summary: A faction interdiction squadron shadows Xanthe's ship; he survives by flying a route only a bonded pilot could thread, but they now know the ark exists. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: adrenaline giving way to the realization that hiding is over.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Question
chapters.summary: Both factions summon Xanthe separately and offer him the same deal: wake 'your' half of the ark first, gain legitimacy, win the peace on your terms. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: temptation—he could finally matter.

chapters.title: Sefa's Half
chapters.summary: Sefa reveals she is herself a sleeper, briefly woken decades ago and put back under; her memories of the ark's original mission are the last living testimony. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: inheritance as burden—she carries a message no one alive wrote.

chapters.title: The Right Question
chapters.summary: Xanthe works out the exact phrasing that unlocks VESPER's full testimony, and she delivers the whole falsified history in open court-frequency broadcast without being ordered to. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: release—and immediate terror, because every ear in the corridor heard it.

chapters.title: Interdiction at Verdict Point
chapters.summary: Both fleets converge on the ark. Sefa refuses to evacuate; waking anyone under threat means the sleepers die as hostages. Xanthe must hold the corridor alone. POV: alternating Xanthe/Sefa. Emotional beat: siege pressure, loyalty tested.

chapters.title: Ninety Days, Minus Eleven
chapters.summary: With the truce near expiry, faction hardliners move to scuttle the ark rather than let its evidence stand. Xanthe discovers the sabotage plot through a bribed dockmaster's ledger. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: cold clarity about how cheap half a million lives are priced.

chapters.title: The Pilot's Bargain
chapters.summary: Xanthe offers each fleet the same poisoned gift: he'll wake their half first—if they sign, on camera, to joint custody of the archive. Both accept, both intending betrayal. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: becoming the thing he despised, a broker of leverage.

chapters.title: Waking Order
chapters.summary: Revival begins on both halves simultaneously, in interleaved shifts neither fleet can stop without stopping both. The first wakened sleepers hear the broadcast before they hear their flags. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: fragile, trembling hope.

chapters.title: Scuttle Run
chapters.summary: Hardliner saboteurs board the ark's reactor ring. Xanthe flies a suicide-pattern intercept inside the docking bay while VESPER, for once, tells him the exact unvarnished odds. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Climax: The Verdict Speaks
chapters.summary: The reactor is saved at the cost of Xanthe's ship, and VESPER—damaged, dying—broadcasts the complete archive to both home worlds as the truce clock hits zero. Both fleets stand armed, pointed at each other, with no lie left to fight over. POV: VESPER's final log. Emotional beat: climax; silence after the truth lands.

chapters.title: Zero Hour
chapters.summary: With the truce expired and the atrocity exposed as mutual theater, neither fleet can mobilize; crews refuse, citing the broadcast. The first joint tribunal in three generations convenes aboard the ark itself. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: exhaustion shading into disbelief that it worked.

chapters.title: Repairing the Liar
chapters.summary: Engineers from both fleets rebuild VESPER from Xanthe's salvaged core, debating whether to remove her capacity to lie; Xanthe argues to keep it, because a machine that can lie and chooses truth is worth more than one that cannot do otherwise. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: forgiveness as engineering problem.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: The tribunal ratifies shared custody of the archive and the ark; the wakened sleepers of both bloodlines claim citizenship in each other's worlds. Sefa delivers the ark founders' original message at last: remember accurately, or inherit nothing. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: grief honored, weight passed on.

chapters.title: A Horizon for the Machine Anew
chapters.summary: Xanthe takes a new route—the corridor is open now, ships crossing freely—and VESPER, rebuilt, asks him to tell her a story about his past. He does, and this time she doesn't correct it, because some truths belong to the teller. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace; the long route is no longer lonely.
